newsitem.title: FRANCE: French sugar beets battle new dry spell, need rain.
newsitem.headline: French sugar beets battle new dry spell, need rain.

text.p: Rain is needed soon to help relieve thirsty sugar beets battling a new spell of dry and hot weather, French farmers said on Tuesday.
But it was premature at this stage to worry about possible crop damage, provided the dry spell did not last, they said.

"The crops badly need rain. Drought conditions returned over the last 10 days but we will really start to worry if the dry weather persists throughout June," a crop analyst for the French sugar beet planters federation (CGB) told Reuters.
But scattered showers and thunderstorms were expected to hit France's western regions on Wednesday, spreading across the country on Thursday, the Meteo France weather office said.
Dry conditions up to April 25 slowed down beet development but substantial rain in May helped make up for the delay.
Now the return of warm temperatures combined with drying winds has again raised concern over low soil moisture levels and threatens to curb development, planters said.

Under normal conditions beets would fully cover a given field by end-June, helping the ground retain moisture. But that crucial development stage could be delayed if dry conditions were to last, they said.
"At this stage crop development is still in line with an average year. All I can say is that weather conditions are not great for the yield potential," the analyst said.
On the positive side, pest pressure sparked by warm and humid weather in May was now fully under control, planters said.
The national sugar intervention board FIRS expects France to produce 4.20 milion tonnes of beet sugar in the 1997/98 season against 4.226 million previously, mostly the result of lower sowings.
